releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.7
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.7.0 ships with `.nvmrc` and `.node-version` support in the global `node` shim, `pnpm install --allow-build`, `pnpm publish --publish-wait-timeout`, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` created from the `workspaces` field. `pnpm install --force` no longer installs optional dependencies built for other platforms. This release also carries security fixes for bin shims on Nix, for lifecycle scripts of packages in a `storeDir` inside the workspace, and for `userAgent` placeholders in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm install --force` now keeps skipping optional dependencies whose `os`, `cpu` or `libc` do not match the host. It still refetches every package and lifts `engineStrict`. The new `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting restores the previous behaviour, installing optional dependencies of every platform under `--force` [#6133](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6133).

- The global `node` shim created by pnpm now uses the Node.js version from the nearest `.nvmrc` or `.node-version` file when the project does not declare a Node.js runtime in `devEngines.runtime` or `engines.runtime` [#4471](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/4471). The nearest directory with a Node.js runtime declaration decides the version. Within one directory, `package.json` takes precedence over `.node-version`, which takes precedence over `.nvmrc`. An `.nvmrc` value that only nvm can act on, such as `system` or a custom alias, is ignored.

- `pnpm install` now supports the `--allow-build` option to selectively allow or deny package lifecycle scripts and record them in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#15388](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15388).

- Added `pnpm publish --publish-wait-timeout <milliseconds>` to wait for published versions and their tarballs to become available from the registry. Set `publishWaitTimeout` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to configure a default. A value of `0` disables the check.

  Recursive publishing confirms availability before publishing dependent packages. If confirmation times out, the command fails.

  When `pnpm publish -r --report-summary` fails after some uploads were accepted, the summary file now lists those packages.

- `pnpm install` now creates `pnpm-workspace.yaml` from the `workspaces` field of the root `package.json` when the repository has no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. The projects the field lists are linked on that same install. An existing `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is never changed. With `--ignore-workspace`, no file is created. If the `workspaces` field later differs from `packages` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, pnpm prints a warning [#2255](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2255).

- When a project pins a pnpm version or a runtime that another pnpm process is installing at that moment, pnpm now waits a few seconds and then installs and runs a private copy of its own. It used to wait up to five minutes and then use the shared install directory without the lock. The private copy is removed once the command has run. `pnpm store prune` rem
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.0 adds the `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting and `pnpm update --peer`, and fixes many bugs in `pnpm deploy`, `--filter`, `nodeLinker: hoisted`, and custom `modulesDir` setups. This release also carries security fixes for shell completion, bin shims on Nix, lifecycle scripts inside a custom `modulesDir`, and `userAgent` placeholders in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

### Minor Changes

* Added the `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting. When it is `false`, `pnpm install --force` skips optional dependencies whose `os`, `cpu` or `libc` do not match the host instead of installing all of them. The default stays `true` [#6133](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6133).

### Patch Changes

#### Security

* pnpm no longer expands environment variables in a `userAgent` set in a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. A `userAgent` with a placeholder in that file is now ignored. Before this fix, pnpm sent the variable's value to the configured registry [#15415](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15415).

* pnpm no longer treats packages inside a custom `modulesDir` as workspace projects, including one that `packageConfigs` sets for a project. Before, with a `modulesDir` such as `vendor` and a `packages` pattern such as `**`, a repeat install ran the lifecycle scripts of dependencies that `allowBuilds` had not approved [#15412](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/15412).

* On Nix, a dependency's bin named like a system utility such as `sed` can no longer redirect a POSIX bin shim or the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers. The shims and launchers now ignore `node_modules` and relative `PATH` entries while they locate their own files. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#14883](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14883).

* Shell completion now omits candidates containing control or invisible formatting characters, and fish completion omits names containing backslashes. Package and script names can no longer inject extra completion records or terminal escape sequences.

* Commands that run pnpm again, such as `pnpm runtime set` and `pnpm env use`, no longer re-run a script that only looks like pnpm. A script named `pnpm` or `pn` that another package installed was run as though it were pnpm.

* `pnpm store prune` now leaves a `dlx` cache root that is a symlink or Windows junction untouched. Cleanup no longer removes directories through that link.

#### Installing packages

* `pnpm install` now fails at once when a registry or tarball server presents a TLS certificate that fails verification, such as a self-signed or expired one. The error names the certificate problem. Such requests were retried for more than a minute [#9134](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9134).

* `pnpm install` no longer appears to hang when a git dependency is fetched over SSH and ssh asks for a key passphrase or a host key confirmation. pnpm now runs ssh in batch mode, so the install fails right away with the ssh error, and a key that needs a passphrase has to be l
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(list): scope default list in workspace package to current project (pnpm/pnpm#14494)
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#14494

Scope default `pnpm list` and `pnpm ll` inside a workspace package directory to the current package rather than the entire workspace.

When run at the workspace root, `pnpm list` remains recursive by default across all workspace projects.
When run inside a workspace package directory without `--recursive` (`-r`) and without `--filter`, it now lists dependencies for that specific package, restoring pnpm v10 behavior. Passing `-r` or `--filter` inside a workspace package continues to run recursively across the workspace or filtered packages.

Implemented in both the TypeScript CLI (`pnpm11/`) and the Rust pacquet CLI (`pnpm/`).

## Squash Commit Body

```text
In pnpm v10, running `pnpm ls` inside a workspace package directory scoped
to that package. Since v11, `list` was marked `recursiveByDefault: true`,
which promoted every `pnpm list` invocation inside a workspace into a
full workspace recursive run unless an explicit filter was supplied.

This changes `main.ts` in TypeScript pnpm v11 and `promote_recursive_by_default`
in Rust pacquet so that `list` and `ll` are only promoted to recursive by default
when executed in the workspace root directory. When executed inside a workspace
member directory without explicit `-r` / `--recursive` or `--filter` flags,
it scopes to the current package.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#14494
```

prs.title: fix(dedupe): prefer the version a catalog: dependency pins
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Turning on `autoDedupe` in this repository (pnpm/pnpm#15505) removed nothing from the lockfile. It moved Jest's `@types/node: '*'` edges from 22.19.19 to 26.6.2, which kept both versions and added a second `jest-config` peer variant.

The cause is the preferred-versions seed. Every direct-dependency spec in a project manifest adds `DIRECT_DEP_SELECTOR_WEIGHT` to the versions it matches, but a `catalog:` spec is not a version, range or tag, so it was skipped. Our projects all get `@types/node` through `catalog:`, so 22.19.19 got no direct-dependency weight. During deduplication every duplicated version has the same lockfile weight, so the tie went to the highest version.

The seed now resolves a `catalog:` spec through the catalogs and seeds the entry it names. A catalog pin now counts the same as the spec written directly in `package.json`, which already worked.

The bug is in both versions:

- v12: `autoDedupe` and `pnpm dedupe`.
- v11: `pnpm dedupe`. v11 has no `autoDedupe`.

Both are fixed here, with a separate changeset for each because the release notes differ.

Tests:

- v12 CLI e2e (`auto_dedupe.rs`): exact and `catalog:` specs, each with `install --auto-dedupe` and with `dedupe`. With the catalog lookup disabled, the `catalog:` cases fail for both commands.
- v12 unit test in `lockfile-preferred-versions`.
- v11 deps-installer test in `catalogs.ts`: fails on the unchanged code.
- v11 unit test in `lockfile.preferred-versions`.

prs.title: fix(pack): bundle dependencies with the isolated linker
prs.author: jdalton
prs.body:
## Summary

Allow `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` to include bundled dependencies with the isolated linker in pnpm v11 and v12, including workspace packages and the dependencies of each bundled package.

Both packlists resolve each bundled dependency from its parent's real directory, the way Node does, so a bundled package's dependencies in `node_modules/.pnpm` are found. The packed location is chosen so Node resolves the same package inside the tarball: the on-disk location when that works, else the top-level `node_modules` unless the root depends on another package of that name, else the parent's own `node_modules`. Resolution starts at the publish directory and never climbs above the workspace root (or the project directory outside a workspace), and a resolved package whose real path leaves that boundary is refused. `pnpm pack` still rejects bundled dependencies with the PnP linker.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#1643.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Include bundled dependencies with the isolated linker in pnpm v11 and v12,
including workspace packages and the dependencies of each bundled package.
Resolve each bundled dependency from its parent's real directory, bounded by
the workspace root or project directory, and pack it where Node resolves it
from the parent's packed location. Keep rejecting bundled dependencies with
the PnP linker. Closes pnpm/pnpm#1643.
```

prs.title: fix(package-requester): respect readPackage hook before checking engineStrict
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

In pnpm v11 with `engineStrict: true` (or `engine-strict=true`), when a dependency specifies strict engine constraints, relaxing `engines` via `.pnpmfile.cjs` (`readPackage` hook) was ignored because `packageIsInstallable` was evaluated on the raw resolved manifest inside `@pnpm/installing.package-requester` before `readPackage` had run in `@pnpm/installing.deps-resolver`.

This PR passes `readPackageHook` into `RequestPackageOptions` so that `packageRequester` runs the hook before checking installability (including `engineStrict`), and tags the package response as hooked so that `resolveDependencies` does not run the hook twice.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15482

## Squash Commit Body

```text
In pnpm v11, packageIsInstallable was evaluated on the raw resolved
manifest inside `@pnpm/installing.package-requester` before the readPackage
hook had a chance to run in `@pnpm/installing.deps-resolver`. When a package
declared strict engine requirements and --engine-strict was enabled,
relaxing engines in .pnpmfile.cjs still failed with
ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE.

Pass readPackageHook into RequestPackageOptions so that packageRequester
runs the hook before validating package installability and tags the response
so resolveDependencies does not run the hook a second time.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15482
```

prs.title: fix(publish): prevent extra metadata probe after publish wait deadline (pnpm/pnpm#15387)
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

In `wait_for_published_packages`, the package probe loop ran inside `tokio::time::timeout` while also sleeping between probe rounds. When the sleep deadline coincided with or slightly trailed the outer timeout deadline (e.g. 100ms timeout with a 100ms sleep), thread descheduling across the deadline could cause tokio's `Timeout` future to poll its inner future first. Because the inner sleep timer had completed, the loop would immediately dispatch a second metadata probe request before the outer timeout was observed, causing flaky test failures expecting exactly 1 request.

This PR computes the deadline once before polling, checks inside the loop whether `now + delay` reaches or exceeds the deadline before sleeping, immediately returns the timeout error if the deadline expired or would expire before the next probe, and caps sleep duration by the remaining time until the deadline.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15387

sleep deadline coincided with or followed the outer timeout deadline,

and launch a second probe before the outer timeout was observed.

- In `@pnpm/store.create-cafs-store`, prioritize `packageImportMethod` when specified over the default hint from `directoryFetcher`.
- Added end-to-end tests for both stacks asserting reporter output, dependency link counts, and that deployed project files remain unlinked across platforms.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#7593

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm deploy` now respects `--package-import-method` passed on the command line.

In TypeScript, `copyProject` now uses disabled logging during project staging so project copying does not preempt the package import method event, and `@pnpm/store.create-cafs-store` prioritizes `packageImportMethod` over the directory fetcher default.

In Rust, `copy_project` suppresses logging with `SilentReporter` so the deploy install emits the accurate import method.
```

prs.title: fix(releasing): private package version bumps
prs.author: puRe1337
prs.body:
## Summary

Private workspace packages now receive pending version bumps without a registry publication check, in both the TypeScript and the Rust CLI.

Since v11.16.0, pnpm checks the npm registry to determine whether a package has already been released. This breaks version bumps for private packages and packages that are not published to an npm registry.

A private package is never published, so in `registry` changelog storage no tarball could ever carry its changelog, and its intent file and parked section stayed in `.changeset/` forever. Its releases now use `repository` storage whatever is configured: the section is prepended to the package's committed `CHANGELOG.md` and the intent is collected at once.

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13519
Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13736

prs.title: fix(setup): replace the alias scripts instead of truncating them
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm setup` failed on Linux with `Text file busy (os error 26)` every time it wrote the alias scripts. The global install that runs first links `$PNPM_HOME/bin/{pn,pnpx,pnx}` as hardlinks of the pnpm executable. `pnpm setup` is that executable, so the `O_TRUNC` open from `fs::write` was refused.

Every alias file (`pn`, `pnpx`, `pnx` and their `.cmd`/`.ps1` wrappers) is now written through the existing `pnpm_fs::write_atomic`. It writes a sibling temp file and renames it over the target, so the busy inode is never opened for writing.

The new test hardlinks the running test binary into `bin/` as all three alias names. That reproduces the real condition, not a simulation of it. Without the fix it fails with `Os { code: 26, kind: ExecutableFileBusy, message: "Text file busy" }`. With the fix it passes.

v11 is not affected. Its global bins are always `cmd-shim` scripts (`globalActivation.ts` never passes `preferSymlinkedExecutables`), so its `writeFileSync` only overwrites a small shell script.

pnpm/pnpm#14663 proposed the same approach, but it predates the current alias-script code and no longer applies. This PR reuses `pnpm_fs::write_atomic` instead of adding another temp-and-rename helper.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15494

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When a package uses `package.yaml` or `package.json5` instead of `package.json`, pnpm did not apply the manifest `files` allowlist. npm-packlist processes the manifest rules only when it finds `package.json` on disk.

- TypeScript (`@pnpm/fs.packlist`): the root walk uses a subclass of npm-packlist's `Walker`. It applies the manifest rules (`files`, `main`, `bin`, and the always-included files) to a package root whose only manifest is `package.yaml` or `package.json5`, and it always includes those manifests alongside `package.json`. Bundled dependencies do not get this, which matches the TypeScript walker. `pnpm-git-fetcher` reads the manifest in any format before computing the packlist.

Separate changesets: v11 covers `pnpm pack` plus git-hosted and injected dependencies. v12 already applied `files` in `pnpm pack`, so its entry covers only git-hosted dependencies.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#7906

prs.title: fix(hoisted): unlink the bins of removed packages
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` removes package directories that the new graph no longer has, but it left the commands those packages linked into `node_modules/.bin`. In the workspace from the issue, a project's nested copy of a package is deduped into the root `node_modules` once every project agrees on its version, and the project's `node_modules/.bin` keeps a command pointing at the deleted copy.

Both stacks now unlink an orphan's commands from its containing `node_modules/.bin` (stepping over the `@scope` dir) before deleting the directory:

- pnpm v12: `remove_orphans` reuses `remove_dep_bins`, the helper the isolated linker's direct-dependency pruning already uses, including its refusal to delete through a `.bin` that is not a real directory.

The bin linking pass after orphan removal re-creates any command that a remaining package in the same `node_modules` still provides.

Reproduced on macOS with pnpm 12.5.1, pnpm 11.27.1, and unmodified `main` builds of both stacks: two workspace projects on `semver` 7.6.0 and 7.5.0, then realigned to 7.6.0. After the second install, `packages/b/node_modules/.bin/semver` was a dangling link. With this change it is gone.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#7568

prs.title: fix(resolver): keep protocol-prefixed range unions away from the npm resolver
prs.author: waltuov
prs.body:
## Summary

A `runtime:` range that contains `||` or a space resolved to the npm package with the same name. The `devEngines.runtime` version `^22.18.0 || ^24.0.0` from the issue installed the npm package `node`, whose build script is not approved by default, so `.bin/node` pointed at a missing file and every script failed. The npm resolver runs first in both resolver chains, and its lenient range parser dropped the `runtime:^22.18.0` member and kept `^24.0.0`.

parseBareSpecifier now declines a selector whose first member contains a colon, in the Rust and the TypeScript stacks. A colon in a later member keeps the old reading, so a merged peer range such as `^1.0.0 || workspace:^2.0.0` still resolves its npm member. Declining every selector with a colon would make that install fail, while pnpm 12.5.1 installs it.

prs.title: fix(cmd-shim): strip node_modules and relative entries from PATH in shims
prs.author: Ayush442842q
prs.body:
## Summary

On Nix, `command -p` falls back to the caller's `PATH`, because no default path is compiled in. A dependency bin named `readlink`, `sed`, or `uname` in `node_modules/.bin` could therefore still redirect a POSIX shim or launcher.

Every POSIX shim header and launcher, in both stacks, now resolves its helpers with a `PATH` that drops `node_modules` segments and relative and empty entries. If nothing survives the filter, the helpers get `/` instead of an empty `PATH`, which would search the current directory. The caller's `PATH` comes back before the target runs. - v12: `SH_SHIM_HEADER` (cmd-shim crate), `RESOLVE_SELF` (`pnpm setup` aliases), and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, `pnx` npm wrapper scripts.
- v11: the `@pnpm/bins.cmd-shim` header, the `pnpm setup` alias scripts, and the `@pnpm/exe` aliases.
- `is_sh_shim_hardened` and v11's `isShimHardened` now pin the filter line, so a warm reinstall replaces pre-fix shims.

prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15528

When a dependency is locked to a prerelease version (e.g. `21.0.0-rc.0`) and `package.json` is updated to a stable version or range (e.g. `21.0.0` or `^21.0.0`), `reusable_importer_dep` and `prior_child_key` previously called `satisfies_with_prereleases`, which stripped the prerelease tag and considered the prerelease version to satisfy the stable range.

This change replaces `satisfies_with_prereleases` with strict `range.satisfies(version)` in lockfile reuse checks so that updating from a prerelease to a stable range re-resolves the dependency.

prs.title: fix(filter): compare [<since>] against the merge base
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#9907.

`--filter "[<since>]"` ran `git diff <since>`, a direct comparison between `<since>` and the working tree. When `<since>` had moved on after the current branch forked from it, projects touched only by those newer commits on `<since>` were selected too. The documented meaning of the selector is "packages changed since the specified commit/branch" ([filtering docs](https://pnpm.io/filtering#--filter-since)), and the common `--filter "...[origin/main]"` use in CI on a feature branch expects the `git diff origin/main...HEAD` view.

Both stacks now diff against `git merge-base <since> HEAD`, with the working tree as the other side, so uncommitted changes are still selected (a plain `<since>...HEAD` range would drop them). When git finds no merge base (a shallow clone missing the fork point, unrelated histories, an invalid or option-like ref), the diff runs against `<since>` as before, so shallow CI checkouts and the existing `bad revision` errors behave exactly as today. When `<since>` is an ancestor of `HEAD` (`[HEAD~1]`, the most common form), the merge base is `<since>` itself and nothing changes.

Reproduced on pnpm 11.27.1, 12.6.0, and a v12 build of `main` (a1b1c8a82f): a repo with `feature` changing `a`, `main` later changing `b`, and an uncommitted edit to `c` selects `a,b,c` for `pnpm list --filter "[main]"`. With the fix, the v12 build and the v11 bundle select `a,c`. In a `--depth 1` clone without the merge base both the fixed and unf

prs.title: fix(workspace-manifest-writer): match existing quote style in pnpm-workspace.yaml for exclude entries (pnpm/pnpm#15079)
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When writing exclude entries (for `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` and `trustPolicyExclude`) to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, pnpm v12 previously always formatted quoted entries with single quotes (e.g. `- '@scope/pkg@1.0.0'`). If the manifest uses double quotes for string scalars, code formatters (such as Prettier or Oxfmt) reformat single quotes to double quotes on formatting passes, resulting in file churn on every install.

This change scans string scalars in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to detect whether double quotes are dominant. When double quotes are dominant, new quoted exclude entries are formatted with double quotes. When single quotes are dominant, or when quote counts are equal or absent, it falls back to single quotes. Plain-safe scalars remain unquoted, and existing exclude entries are preserved verbatim.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15079

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Detect the dominant quote style of string scalars in pnpm-workspace.yaml when writing or updating exclude entries (minimumReleaseAgeExclude and trustPolicyExclude). If double quotes are dominant, format new quoted exclude entries with double quotes to avoid churn with formatters such as Prettier or Oxfmt. Fall back to single quotes if single quotes dominate or if counts are equal or absent.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15079
```

When an npm registry returns package metadata with tarball URLs containing explicit default ports (e.g. `https://registry.npmjs.org:443/...` or `http://registry.example.com:80/...`), pacquet previously retained the default port in `picked_tarball_resolution`. prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm add`, `remove`, and `update` rewrite `package.json` from the parsed value, which drops blank lines that separate entries. This keeps them. Closes pnpm/pnpm#5602.

On read, pnpm records which object members have blank lines in front of them, keyed by the member's path (for example `scripts` > `foo`). prs.author: MisterJimson
prs.body:
## Summary

Refs pnpm/pnpm#7826

`pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now warn when the tarball includes a `.env` or `.env.*` file that the manifest's `files` field does not name. Templates (`.env.example`, `.env.sample`, `.env.template`) are not reported. The tarball contents are unchanged.

The PR first excluded `.env` from the packlist unconditionally in both stacks. That approach was dropped:

- npm (`npm-packlist`), Yarn Berry (`plugin-pack`) and Bun all pack a plain `.env`. Bun ignores only `.env.production`, and `files` can re-include it. Silent exclusion would make pnpm produce different tarballs from every other client.
- The packlist also selects files for git, directory and tarball dependencies, so the exclusion changed installs as well as pack.
- There was no way to ship a `.env` on purpose.

The warning goes in pnpm v12 only, since it is a new behavior. The plan is to make it an error in pnpm v13. A file counts as listed when a `files` entry whose last segment starts with `.env` matches its packed path, using the packlist's own `files` matcher (`.env`, `**/.env`, `config/.env*`). A directory entry such as `dist` that merely contains the file does not count.

Under `pack --json` the warning is not printed, because that reporter drops every non-lifecycle event to keep stdout valid JSON.

.env.* file that no files entry names, directly or through a dotenv glob.

prs.author: Shuuren
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm install` honors `Cache-Control` for a dependency named with an `http:` or `https:` tarball URL. A fresh response is taken from the store with no request, and a stale one is revalidated with `If-None-Match`.

URL tarball resolution kept no URL to integrity record outside the lockfile, so a lockfile-less install always sent `HEAD` and `GET`. The resolver now stores that record under `<cacheDir>/v11/tarball-resolutions`, with the response's `ETag`, `Cache-Control`, and its initial age from `Age` and `Date`. A record whose archive is gone from the store is dropped. Responses fetched with credentials, for the requested URL or its immutable redirect target, are not recorded.

This is a new capability, so it lands in pnpm v12 only.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15648

The Rust install test `fresh_remote_tarball_skips_the_network_without_a_lockfile` repeats an install with `lockfile: false` and asserts the second install sends no request while the response is fresh. `stale_remote_tarball_revalidates_with_if_none_match` expires that record and asserts the next install sends `If-None-Match` and accepts `304`. Unit tests cover case-insensitive directives, invalid `max-age`, and `Age`/`Date` counting toward freshness.

This pull request was written with AI assistance.

A lockfile-less install sent HEAD and GET for a URL tarball on every run because resolution had no URL to integrity record
